title: Firefighters free a 3-year-old from a septic pipe in West Goshen
summary: West Chester Fire Department and West Goshen police crews pulled a young boy out of a narrow septic access pipe on Snyder Avenue Tuesday evening after about 25 minutes. He was taken to a hospital and did not appear to be hurt.

title: Kennett schools roll out live bus tracking for families
summary: Kennett Consolidated School District launched the free Stopfinder app this week, letting parents see bus locations on a map and set arrival alerts for stops and schools. Registration invitations went out to families starting Oct. 26.
loc: Kennett Consolidated School District, Kennett Square

title: Evening Halloween Parade draws more than a thousand downtown
summary: Wednesday's 7 p.m. parade, moved back from last year's afternoon slot, ran about 40 minutes behind the police color guard, with marching bands including WCU's Golden Rams playing "Thriller" and packed outdoor dining along the route.

title: West Pikeland puts the SALT Performing Arts building sale on hold
summary: Supervisors voted unanimously Oct. 26 to reverse last week's decision to sell the township building the theater has renovated and occupied since 2014, while they get legal advice on requiring any buyer to honor SALT's license. SALT is also exploring an acquisition with Historic Yellow Springs.

title: Hatfield bacon family's developer buys Downingtown's Mill Town Square
summary: Clemens Development paid $22.4 million for the 104,000-square-foot shopping center anchored by Planet Fitness and Kimberton Whole Foods, ending a 24-year ownership by Tripoint Properties.

title: State EV grant funds on-street chargers in West Chester
summary: PennDOT's new $37 million NEVI award round pays for 23 on-street Level 2 charging ports shared by West Chester, Phoenixville and Malvern. A separate $550,600 grant adds four DC fast chargers at the Let's Go Mart in West Chester.

title: Westtown star Jordyn Palmer commits to South Carolina
summary: The five-star senior, a three-time Gatorade Pennsylvania Player of the Year, chose Dawn Staley's Gamecocks over more than 20 programs including UCLA and Penn State.

title: Sitara Indian Cuisine opens on Lancaster Avenue in Malvern
summary: The new restaurant serves tandoor and tiffin-style dishes along with Indo-Chinese noodle and rice plates.

title: Boutique On Thirty closing in Downingtown
summary: The Downingtown boutique is shutting down roughly a year after it opened.

title: Brandywine Museum's $30 million floodproofing work nears completion
summary: Five years after Hurricane Ida flooded Brandywine Creek to a record 21 feet, the Chadds Ford museum has sealed off about 12,000 square feet of its lower levels and rerouted its systems behind flood barriers. Crews also took out the upstream Hoffman's Mill Dam this month to ease the creek's flow.
loc: Brandywine Museum of Art, Chadds Ford
